- [USER] User inquired about specific speeches or statements made by Lloyd George on the topic of women's suffrage.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lloyd George stated: "I believe that women have a right to vote on equal terms with men. I do not think that the possession of a vote is a matter for one sex alone." (1910)
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lloyd George stated: "Women’s suffrage will be won. It is only a matter of time." (1912)
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lloyd George stated: "The Government is sympathetically disposed to the claims of the women." (1913)
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lloyd George stated: "We have passed beyond the stage where the discrimination of man against woman can be tolerated." (1915)
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lloyd George stated: "I hope that the time is not far distant when the suffrage will be extended to those who help to bear the burdens of the state, to those who have served it in the field, and to those who have laboured for it in the workshop." (1917)
- [USER] User asked if Lloyd George actively worked to support women's suffrage or was just voicing his opinions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lloyd George actively worked to support women's suffrage throughout his political career.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] As Chancellor of the Exchequer, Lloyd George introduced a proposal for women's suffrage in 1912, which would have given the vote to women who owned property or were married to property owners.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The proposal for women's suffrage introduced by Lloyd George in 1912 was defeated.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In 1913, Lloyd George gave a speech in support of the suffrage movement and promised to introduce a new suffrage bill if the current one failed.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lloyd George worked behind the scenes to persuade other politicians to support the cause of women's suffrage.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] During World War I, Lloyd George became Prime Minister and used his position to push for women's suffrage.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Representation of the People Act was passed in 1918, giving women over the age of 30 who met certain property qualifications the right to vote.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Overall, Lloyd George was a strong supporter of women's suffrage and worked actively to make it a reality.
